speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) whether there is a remuneration cap for key management staff of Fifth Schedule companies like GIC and Temasek Holdings; and (b) for the past five years, what is the range of total annual remuneration, including salary, annual and performance bonuses, paid to the top three higher paid executives in GIC and Temasek respectively.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Instead, we hold the boards accountable for their respective performances.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The salaries are benchmarked to the relevant markets and sectors where the entities compete for talent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This ensures that they can attract and retain capable people.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The remuneration frameworks also aim to support and reinforce a prudent risk-taking culture.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This ensures that staff, including senior management, are rewarded for long-term sustained performance, rather than a focus on short-term gains.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: These figures are published in their annual reports, and they show that both GIC and Temasek have performed creditably under challenging market conditions.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The reason I asked is because these two entities are managing our Reserves and the Government is the sole shareholder.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Usually, the shareholders would know the remuneration packages for the company that they own.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Does the Government or anyone in the Finance Ministry know the remuneration packages for the top brass in terms of the value of GIC and Temasek?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, our focus should not be on one or two expense items, but on designing an overall system that enhances and maximises long-term performance, and that is what we have tried to do.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As I have explained in this House before, the way we go about this is through a very rigorous process.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: When we look at expected future long-term returns, there is a thorough assessment of the investment environment, done by professionals.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Ministry of Finance reviews that assessment of the investment environment.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That overall system is designed, as I have said, to maximise and secure our best chances of getting good long-term returns.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is the system we have today which achieves that result.
